Br. MSME-DFO, Itanagar Empowers PM Vishwakarma Artisans through Branding & Marketing Awareness Programme
articles.full_content:
The Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, Government of India, through the Branch MSME Development and Facilitation Office, Itanagar, organised a one-day awareness programme under the PM Vishwakarma Scheme at DIC Yupia in Papumpare district, Arunachal Pradesh, on 8 September 2026. The workshop was graced by Shri Dasher Taba Aka, DDI (DIC), Shri Vijay Sehrawat, Assistant Director, Branch MSME-DFO, Shri Lindam Rana, President, APM & SIDA, Shri Pradip Das, LDM (SBI), Shri Parma Mahato, Postal Assistant, Smt. Techi Mana, Udyam Mitra, DIC, Yupia and Smt. Anushree Choudhury (SLPMU-PMV).
The programme was organised in association with the Department of Industries, Government of Arunachal Pradesh, and the APM&SIDA. It aimed to strengthen the entrepreneurial and marketing capabilities of PM Vishwakarma artisans by providing practical knowledge on product development, branding, market access and the use of emerging digital technologies. The awareness programme was attended by more than 80 participants.
Shri. D.T. Aka inaugurated the session with an overview of the workshop, followed by Shri Lindam Rana shared his local demographics and the entrepreneurial opportunity in Arunachal Pradesh.
Shri. Vijay Sehrawat emphasized on the implementation of PM Vishwakarma and its wide scope in terms of upskilling, entrepreneurial opportunities, trade fairs and exhibitions, technology and innovation, branding, loan and subsidies etc. The participants were further informed about relevant schemes of the Ministry of MSME and the Government of Arunachal Pradesh that may support enterprise growth and market expansion. The workshop also emphasized on inclusion and linkage of Vishwakarma beneficiaries with Social Security schemes. Awareness was also generated regarding export promotion opportunities for products made by PM Vishwakarma beneficiaries.
Smt. Anushree Choudhury conducted sessions on entrepreneurship, pricing, market trends, sales, financial and digital literacy, packaging, labelling, branding, and e-commerce onboarding. Artisans were introduced to AI tools for product branding, content creation, marketing, and customer engagement. Through practical discussions, participants learned improved packaging, pricing, design, and digital marketing techniques, highlighting how technology and modern business practices can help artisans expand market access and build sustainable enterprises.
The programme by Shri. Pradip Das discussed on financial literacy and financial inclusion, covering access to formal banking services and social security measures such as loan application and disbursement process.
The workshop also had a brief session on export and DNK services by Shri. Parma Mahato, followed by Udyam Registration, the Udyam Assist Platform and QR-code generation, with the objective of improving the formalisation and digital market readiness of artisans by Smt. Techi Mana.

Media Workshop Vartalap in Berhampore highlights Ayushman Bharat, PM Jan Dhan Yojana, PM Awas Yojana, Swachh Bharat Yojana, PM Surya Ghar and other Government Initiatives
articles.full_content:
Berhampore, Murshidabad, September 9, 2026
Press Information Bureau (PIB), Kolkata, organised a media workshop 'Vartalap' in Berhampore, Murshidabad, today, aiming at strengthening engagement with grassroots level journalists and facilitating effective dissemination of information on government initiatives and development programmes. The programme focused on key issues including Ayushman Bharat, Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana, Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT), child trafficking and other development initiatives of the Union Government.
Addressing the gathering, the Director General (Eastern Zone), PIB and CBC, Shri T. V. K. Reddy, emphasised the importance of PIB Vartalap in establishing a direct interface with journalists working at the grassroots level. He highlighted the role of journalists in ensuring that authentic and verified information reaches people, particularly in rural and underserved areas. Shri Reddy also spoke about the Press and Registration of Periodicals Act, 2023 and the Press Sewa Portal, which facilitates smoother registration and processing for periodicals. He the urged journalists to make effective use of the PIB website as a reliable source of information for professional and development-oriented journalism.
The Minister for Mass Education Extension and Library Services and Backward Classes Welfare, Government of West Bengal, Shri Gouri Sankar Ghosh, stressed the importance of disseminating fact-based and authentic news. He highlighted the significance of major government initiatives such as Ayushman Bharat, Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana and Swachh Bharat Yojana, and emphasised the need for effective implementation of government schemes so that their benefits reach the intended beneficiaries.
Speaking on healthcare initiatives, the Chief Medical Officer of Health, Murshidabad, Dr. Sandip Sanyal, underlined the importance of effective information dissemination regarding government health initiatives. He explained the process of availing benefits under Ayushman Bharat and urged journalists to create awareness among beneficiaries regarding e-KYC and facilitate informed access to the scheme through responsible dissemination of information. He also highlighted the importance of the ABHA ID and digital health records, besides discussing maternal health programmes and initiatives for the eradication of tuberculosis. The session was followed by an interactive question-and-answer session.
The Lead District Manager, Punjab National Bank, Shri Fajal Mamud, elaborated on the significance of Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana and Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) in promoting financial inclusion. He projected the financial inclusion achievements in the Murshidabad district of West Bengal and the role of such initiatives in ensuring greater access to formal banking services, including for women and other sections of society. He also spoke about Pradhan Mantri Surya Ghar, Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana and Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY

Union Budget 2026-27 Accelerating Chhattisgarh's Inclusive Development and Economic Growth: Shri Ramdas Athawale
articles.full_content:
Union Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment reviews welfare schemes and central flagship initiatives in Raipur
Union Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment, Shri Ramdas Athawale, addressed the media during his official visit to Chhattisgarh, highlighting that the Union Budget 2026-27 is providing a strong financial impetus to the state's all-round development under the vision of 'Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas, Sabka Vishwas, Sabka Prayas'. The Union Minister noted that a tax devolution of ₹50,427 crore has been proposed for Chhattisgarh in the Union Budget, alongside a grant provision of ₹15,000 crore for FY 2025-26 to bolster the state's financial capability and infrastructure works. Presenting the progress of central flagship schemes in the state, Shri Athawale stated that central social security and welfare programs are creating a transformative impact on rural, poor, and tribal communities across Chhattisgarh.
Under the Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana, more than 1.88 crore bank accounts have been opened in the state, securing financial inclusion with deposits amounting to over ₹9,324 crore. Furthermore, over 39.75 lakh gas connections have been allotted in Chhattisgarh under the Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana, providing clean cooking fuel to rural households. Highlighting infrastructure and health developments, the Minister underlined that approval for 5 new medical colleges has been granted to expand medical education and healthcare infrastructure in the state.
Additionally, an Indian Oil bottling plant constructed at a cost of over ₹130 crore in Korba is driving logistics, local employment, and energy security in the region. Under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (Urban), over 1.77 lakh houses have been constructed with an allocation of ₹4,699 crore, while under the Ujala Scheme, 1.08 crore LED bulbs have been distributed across the state.
The Union Minister re-affirmed the Central Government's focus on the welfare of marginalized communities, adding that funding has been provided for 5 De-addiction Centres and 3 Old Age Homes in the region to support social defense initiatives. Earlier in the day, Shri Athawale chaired a high-level review meeting with senior officials of the Chhattisgarh government and the Raipur Municipal Corporation to assess the implementation of social welfare programs and review the progress of SC/ST backlog recruitment.

The Union Minister noted that a tax devolution of ₹50,427 crore has been proposed for Chhattisgarh in the Union Budget, alongside a grant provision of ₹15,000 crore for FY 2025-26 to bolster the state's financial capability and infrastructure works. Presenting the progress of central flagship schemes in the state, Shri Athawale stated that central social security and welfare programs are creating a transformative impact on rural, poor, and tribal communities across Chhattisgarh.

MSDE Organises ‘Skill Manthan’ on 'Building Sustainable Livelihoods for Women'
articles.full_content:
Districts are the engines of economic growth and reform : Shri Jayant Chaudhary at the inaugural session of ‘Skill Manthan’
The Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE), Government of India, organised the inaugural session of ‘ Skill Manthan’ centred on the theme ‘Building Sustainable Livelihoods for Women’. The virtual dialogue highlighted innovative initiatives from Meerut and Bijnor in Uttar Pradesh and NTR District in Andhra Pradesh, demonstrating how district administrations can combine skilling, entrepreneurship, finance, technology, and market access to create sustainable livelihood opportunities for women. ‘Skill Manthan’ will serve as a knowledge-sharing platform to showcase innovative and impactful district-led initiatives.
Speaking on the initiative, Shri Jayant Chaudhary, Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Skill Development and Entrepreneurship and Minister of State for Education, Government of India, said, “District administrations are the true engines of growth, reform and transformation. Through our district-led planning approach, we are ensuring that skilling initiatives are driven by local needs and aligned with the requirements of industry, particularly MSMEs. Supported by District Skill Development Plans, the skilling agenda is at the forefront of district administration, enabling more responsive, demand-driven and impactful outcomes for youth and local economies.”
Smt. Debashree Mukherjee, Secretary, MSDE, said, “India’s skilling aspirations can only be realised when skill development is driven by local realities. Hyperlocal skilling, aligned to district needs and employment opportunities, is essential to equip our youth with relevant skills and connect them to meaningful livelihoods in a rapidly evolving economy.”
District Collectors and District Magistrates, Ms. Jasjit Kaur of Bijnor, Uttar Pradesh, Dr. G. Lakshmisha of NTR, Andhra Pradesh and Dr. Vijay Kumar Singh of Meerut, Uttar Pradesh showcased innovative pathways for women’s economic empowerment through skilling, entrepreneurship, and market integration. Meerut demonstrated a women-centric manufacturing model that provides hands-on training and employment in badminton racket and shuttlecock production. Bijnor highlighted Vidur Prerna Swadeshi, a district-wide platform enabling rural women entrepreneurs through branding, market access, and enterprise support. NTR District’s RISE showcased a one-stop ecosystem offering skilling, credit facilitation, mentoring, employment linkages, and entrepreneurial support, illustrating how local institutions can be converged to create sustainable opportunities for women-led enterprises.
The session reaffirmed MSDE’s commitment to strengthening collaboration with district administrations and creating a national platform for documenting, sharing, and replicating successful grassroots models. Self-assembly of organic molecules opens a new path to green hydrogen production
articles.full_content:
A simple yet powerful strategy of integrating naturally occurring amino acid with a light-absorbing organic molecule could improve solar driven hydrogen production using completely metal free organic materials.
Hydrogen is considered one of the most promising clean energy carriers because its combustion produces only water, making it an environmentally benign alternative to fossil fuels. One of the promising methods for producing green hydrogen is by using sunlight to split water into hydrogen and oxygen. However, most existing photocatalysts rely on inorganic semiconductors or precious metals, which are often expensive, difficult to manufacture, and raise concerns regarding long-term sustainability. Developing efficient metal-free organic photocatalysts has therefore remained a major scientific challenge.
A team of researchers from the Centre for Nano and Soft Matter Sciences (CeNS), Bengaluru, -an autonomous institute under Department of Science and Technology (DST), integrated a naturally occurring amino acid (aspartic acid) with a light-absorbing organic molecule, perylene diimide (PDI) and allowed the molecules to spontaneously organize themselves through supramolecular self-assembly.
They found that the enhanced performance arises from how the molecule organizes itself. The amino acid moiety promotes strong, extended hydrogen bonding, while the PDI chromophore drives π–π stacking and efficient light absorption.
Thus, the synergistic interplay between the two governs the molecular organization and, consequently, the functional properties of the material.
The researchers synthesised an aspartic acid-functionalized perylene diimide (PDI) molecule that spontaneously self-assembled in water into highly ordered two-dimensional nanosheets.
This subtle molecular reorganization dramatically broadened light absorption, enhanced charge separation, reduced energy losses, and increased the accessible surface area for catalytic reactions without altering the molecule's chemical composition. As a result, the self-assembled material generated nearly 18% higher photocurrent than its bulk counterpart during solar-driven water splitting.
Advanced electrochemical measurements together with density functional theory (DFT)
calculations further revealed that self-assembly promotes more efficient charge transport, while the amino acid increases the molecular dipole moment, facilitating effective separation of photo-generated charges that drive hydrogen evolution.
The study further demonstrates that naturally occurring amino acids can serve not only as molecular building blocks but also as powerful regulators of supramolecular organization and photocatalytic performance. This molecular design strategy offers a sustainable route to developing efficient, environmentally friendly, and metal-free photocatalysts for solar energy conversion.

Active participation of public representatives and citizens at the grassroots level essential to address solid waste management: Dr Parag Madhukar Dhakate, Member Secretary, Pollution Control Board
articles.full_content:
- Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026 emphasise four-stream segregation, digital monitoring and accountability of Bulk Waste Generators - Focus on taking scientific and data-driven approaches to the grassroots and strengthening the leadership role of public representatives - Effective monitoring and online tracking mechanism from Gram Panchayat to the central level - 100 per cent door-to-door waste collection in all 1,314 wards of Uttarakhand - Target to accelerate legacy waste treatment and dumpsite remediation in Uttarakhand by December 2026 - Special solid waste management plan for Char Dham and tourism areas emphasised: Shri Praveen Kumar, Additional Director, Urban Development
A press conference on ‘Solid Waste Management’ was organised by the Press Information Bureau (PIB), Dehradun, under the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, Government of India, at the Secretariat Media Centre on Wednesday. Detailed information was shared on the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026, dumpsite remediation, waste segregation, air pollution control and the role of local bodies.
Dr Parag Madhukar Dhakate, Member Secretary, Pollution Control Board, said that the quantity of waste is increasing with rapid urbanisation. In this context, it is essential to take scientific and data-driven approaches to the grassroots level and ensure the active participation of public representatives and citizens. The goals of effective solid waste management and clean air can be achieved not through government efforts alone, but through collective participation.
He said that under the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026, which came into effect from 1 April 2026, emphasis has been placed on segregating waste into four streams—wet, dry, sanitary and special-care waste. The responsibilities of Bulk Waste Generators (BWGs) have also been strengthened, with a provision for Extended Bulk Waste Generators Responsibility (EBWGR). The Rules provide for online monitoring of waste collection, transportation, processing and disposal, along with digital registration and reporting. The objective is to enhance transparency and accountability, promote the use of waste as a resource and strengthen the circular economy. Recycling and reuse have been prioritised, while landfill has been kept as the last resort.
Dr Dhakate emphasised that 100 per cent door-to-door waste collection is being provided across 1,314 wards under 108 Urban Local Bodies in Uttarakhand. Around 1,515 vehicles are currently available, while procurement of additional vehicles is underway. New vehicles are being equipped with four compartments for four-stream segregation. Source segregation has already been initiated in 1,225 wards. Approximately 1,930.85 metric tonnes of waste is generated daily in the state, of which 1,804.59 metric tonnes (93.46 per cent) is processed every day. Press Information Bureau, Nagpur to Organise VARTALAP on “Skill Development and Future Opportunities: The Role of Regional Media in Spreading Public Awareness” in Buldhana
articles.full_content:
Nagpur/Buldhana : 8 September 2026
The Press Information Bureau (PIB), Nagpur, will organise a VARTALAP – Media Conference for journalists from Buldhana district on 09 September 2026 at Buldhana Residency, Ganesh Nagar, Malkapur Road, Buldhana, from 10 am to 3 pm. The workshop will focus on the theme “Skill Development and Future Opportunities: The Role of Regional Media in Spreading Public Awareness.”
The inaugural session will be held in the presence of prominent officers from the Buldhana district.
The workshop aims to strengthen awareness among media professionals about emerging opportunities in skill development, tourism, sustainable development and Government initiatives, while highlighting the important role of the media in creating awareness and aspirations and disseminating accurate information among citizens.
The technical sessions will focus on sectors and issues relevant to Buldhana's development and future potential.
The programme will also feature a special session on “Role of the Press Information Bureau in Disseminating Information to the Print, Electronic and Digital Media on Government Policies, Programmes, Initiatives and Achievements, Journalist Welfare Scheme and PIB Fact Check.”
The programme will also include an interaction between beneficiaries of Central Sector Schemes and media representatives, providing an opportunity for journalists to gain first-hand insights into the impact of Government initiatives at the grassroots level.
Designed for professionals from the print, electronic and digital media, the VARTALAP Media Workshop will promote dialogue, knowledge sharing and capacity building among journalists. The programme will also provide an opportunity for media professionals to engage with subject experts, Government officials and beneficiaries, thereby strengthening informed, accurate and responsible reporting on issues of public importance.

articles.summary: Nagpur/Buldhana : 8 September 2026 The Press Information Bureau (PIB), Nagpur, will organise a VARTALAP – Media Conference for journalists from Buldhana district on 09 September 2026 at Buldhana Residency, Ganesh Nagar, Malkapur Road, Buldhana, from 10 am to 3 pm. The workshop will focus on the theme “Skill Development and Future Opportunities: The Role of Regional Media in Spreading Public Awareness.” The inaugural session will be held in the presence of prominent officers from the Buldhana district. The workshop aims to strengthen awareness among media professionals about emerging opportunities in skill development, tourism, sustainable development and Government initiatives, while highlighting the important role of the media in creating awareness and aspirations and disseminating accurate information among citizens.

Shri. Sibi Adhithya Senthil Kumar, IAS., District Collector, Cuddalore inaugurates New Aadhaar Seva Kendra
articles.full_content:
Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI) operationalized a new state-of-the art Aadhaar Seva Kendra (ASK) at Cuddalore, on Tuesday, 08th September 2026 marking another step towards strengthening residentcentric Aadhaar services in the city of Cuddalore. The ASK Cuddalore was inaugurated by Thiru. Sibi Adhithya Senthil Kumar, IAS., District Collector of Cuddalore as a Chief Guest, in the presence of Director, Tamil Nadu, UIDAI RO Bengaluru and other officials, M/s BLS and ASK Staff among others.
The District Collector appreciated the UIDAI’s effort and interacted with residents who visited ASK as well as the centre staff present there. Also, enquired about the Aadhaar enrolment and update procedures, and reviewed the various Aadhaar services being provided at the centre. The ASK Cuddalore is equipped with 8 operational kits to provide seamless Aadhaar-related services to thousands of residents. The ASK is functional on all days except public holidays, thereby ensuring greater accessibility & convenience. The Aadhaar Seva Kendra offers Aadhaar enrolment, demographic and biometric updates, grievance redressal and other Aadhaar related services under one roof. In addition to the enrolment and update transactions, ASK Cuddalore will also receive grievances from Aadhaar number holders for their resolution through the Regional Office. With the inauguration of the Aadhaar Seva Kendra (ASK) at Cuddalore, UIDAI has now operationalised 15 Aadhaar Seva Kendras across Tamil Nadu. A further 15 ASKs are scheduled to become operational in the coming days across various districts, increasing the total 30 UIDAI-run Aadhaar Seva Kendras in the State. The ASKs run by UIDAI, are designed to be fully inclusive and resident-friendly with facilities such as wheelchair accessibility, accessible restrooms, and a dedicated grievance redressal mechanism. Residents can also book appointments online for Aadhaar services at ASKs through UIDAI’s appointment portal: https://bookappointment.uidai.gov.in/ .

“Kerala and Uttar Pradesh Can Collaborate in Tourism, Investment and Skill Development”: Invest UP CEO
articles.full_content:
Media delegation from Keralam meets CEO, Invest UP
Lucknow, 8 September 2026: A media delegation from Keralam on a press tour to Uttar Pradesh, organised by the Press Information Bureau (PIB), Thiruvananthapuram, interacted with Shri. Vijay Kiran Anand IAS, Chief Executive Officer of Invest UP in Lucknow. The interaction focused on Uttar Pradesh’s industrial transformation, investment opportunities, infrastructure, tourism, skill development and possible areas of cooperation with Keralam.
The CEO said Uttar Pradesh, with a population of around 250 million and a young workforce, had witnessed significant transformation over the past decade. The State has eight operational expressways, with eight more under development, along with industrial clusters and land banks along major connectivity corridors. Fourteen airports are operational, with further expansion underway, including the Jewar airport. Around ₹2 lakh crore has been invested in infrastructure, including expressways, railways, industrial areas and logistics facilities.
The State’s Gross State Domestic Product has grown from around ₹12 lakh crore to nearly ₹33 lakh crore in nine years and is expected to cross ₹36 lakh crore. Manufacturing has recorded growth of around 15–20 per cent over the past five years. The number of factories established annually has increased from around 500 a decade ago to 4,300 last year, while exports have crossed ₹2 lakh crore.
With around 96 lakh MSMEs, Uttar Pradesh has significant potential in food processing, agro-processing, dairy, animal husbandry and other sectors. The One District One Product initiative was highlighted as an important component of the State’s MSME ecosystem.
The State is following a cluster-based approach to industrial development. Around 12,500 acres are available for industrial clusters along expressways, while 5,000 acres are being developed under the Defence Industrial Corridor. A further 50,000-acre industrial area is being developed in Bundelkhand. The Yamuna Expressway Authority area near Jewar airport is emerging as a major industrial hub, with nearly 3,000 industrial units already allotted and developed.
Electronics, IT, data centres, AI, deep technology, robotics, semiconductors, pharmaceuticals, textiles, leather, footwear, automobiles, electric vehicles and defence are among the focus sectors. Noida has emerged as a major electronics manufacturing centre, while six nodes of the Defence Industrial Corridor have attracted more than 100 companies.
The CEO said services and Global Capability Centres (GCCs) were emerging as key areas of focus. Noida has around 200 GCCs and 200 IT companies, while Lucknow is developing as another services hub with companies including IBM, HCL, Genpact and TCS.
Tourism was identified as an important area for Keralam–Uttar Pradesh cooperation. The State is developing spiritual, Buddhist and other tourism circuits covering destinations such as Varanasi, Ayodhya, Prayagraj, Chitrakoot, Agra and Lucknow.

Vijay Kiran Anand IAS, Chief Executive Officer of Invest UP in Lucknow. The interaction focused on Uttar Pradesh’s industrial transformation, investment opportunities, infrastructure, tourism, skill development and possible areas of cooperation with Keralam.

MoSPI held Workshop on Data Harmonisation for Use of Administrative Data in Data Driven Governance
articles.full_content:
Pr. Secretary-2 to the PM: Trusted, timely and interoperable data is essential for evidence-based policymaking and data-driven governance Secretary MeitY: Availability of high-quality data is fundamental to the successful deployment of AI for governance Secretary, MoSPI: Harmonised, quality-assured and well-documented data is fundamental to an AI-ready government
The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) organized a Workshop of Statistical Advisers (SAs) and Chief Data Officers of all Central Government Ministries, Departments and Organisations (MDOs) on September 08, 2026 at Rang Bhawan Auditorium, Akashwani Bhawan, Broadcasting House, Parliament Street, New Delhi – 110001 on the theme “Data Harmonisation for Use of Administrative Data in Data Driven Governance.” The workshop was aimed at strengthening the National Data System , promoting effective use and harmonisation of administrative data , and fostering greater coordination for data-driven governance and evidence-based policymaking across Government.
The inaugural session was graced by Shri Shaktikanta Das, Principal Secretary-2 to the Prime Minister, Shri S. Krishnan, Secretary, MeitY, Dr. Saurabh Garg, Secretary, MoSPI and Shri P. R. Meshram, Director General (Data Governance), MoSPI . The meeting was attended by Statistical Advisers, Chief Data Officers as well as other senior officers and other representatives from various Central Ministries/Departments of Government of India.
The Chief Guest, Shri Shaktikanta Das launched the Quarterly Progress Report (QPR) portal on Data Harmonisation (https://qpr.mospi.gov.in). The QPR Portal is a technology-enabled platform for use by all Central MDOs to report progress in identification and cataloguing of datasets made ready for dissemination, its metadata preparation, use of national and international standards, classifications and common unique identifiers in machine readable data, and performing quality checks as per Statistical Quality Assurance Framework (SQAF) by respective MDO. The QPR portal has automated validation, dashboards, cross-verification with the NMDS web portal and shall provide analytical insights across Ministries, Departments and Organisations
In his Keynote address, Shri Shaktikanta Das emphasised that trusted, timely and interoperable data is essential for evidence-based policymaking and data-driven governance. He called for greater use of administrative data and statistical expertise across Ministries/Departments for policy formulation, monitoring and outcome assessment. Key MoSPI initiatives, including NMDS 2.0, SQAF, statistical classifications, data lifecycle guidelines, e-Sankhyiki, Microdata Portal and QPR on Data Harmonisation , were highlighted as important enablers of a stronger administrative data ecosystem. He urged all Ministries/Departments to establish Data Governance Committees, publish data-sharing frameworks, maintain live dataset inventories and leverage existing national data-sharing

The inaugural session was graced by Shri Shaktikanta Das, Principal Secretary-2 to the Prime Minister, Shri S. Meshram, Director General (Data Governance), MoSPI .

Bharat Renewable Energy Summit 2026 Roadshow Reaches Bengaluru Highlighting Karnataka and Southern India’s Clean Energy Ecosystem
articles.full_content:
The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy organizes the fifth regional roadshow for the Bharat Renewable Energy Summit and Expo (BRESE) 2026 in Bengaluru focusing on Karnataka’s scale, innovation, and leadership in the clean energy transition. Karnataka aims to add 10 GW of capacity by 2027 under its Integrated Renewable Energy Policy 2025 and targets ₹50,000 crore in investments via the Clean Mobility Policy 2025–30.
Building on the momentum of previous regional sessions held in Jaipur, Mumbai, Hyderabad, and Ahmedabad, the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) successfully organized the fifth roadshow for the Bharat Renewable Energy Summit and Expo 2026 today in Bengaluru. Organized in partnership with the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) and moderated by the International Solar Alliance (ISA), the event brought Karnataka’s scale in clean energy, technological innovation, and industrial leadership into national focus ahead of the main summit scheduled for November in New Delhi.
Addressing the gathering, Shri K.J. George, Hon’ble Minister of Energy, Government of Karnataka, highlighted that India’s renewable energy transition has evolved into a crucial engine for economic growth, employment generation, and energy security. As the nation crosses 300 GW of non-fossil fuel-based installed capacity toward its 500 GW target by 2030, he emphasized Karnataka’s role as a vital partner in this mission. He cited the Pavagada Solar Park as a successful model of inclusive, community-backed development and invited global investors, developers, and manufacturers to collaborate with the state to accelerate clean energy expansion.
Shri Gaurav Gupta, Additional Chief Secretary, Energy Department, Government of Karnataka, outlined the state’s strategic focus on policy execution, streamlined land leasing, transmission infrastructure strengthening, and proactive industry engagement. He noted that under the Integrated Renewable Energy Policy 2025, Karnataka aims to add 10 GW of capacity by 2027 while leveraging its massive 155 GW potential. He further detailed that Karnataka is actively promoting Green Energy Corridors and Renewable Energy Parks through Public-Private Partnership (PPP) models, alongside an ambitious ₹7.5 lakh crore investment and 20 lakh jobs target embedded within its Industrial Policy 2025–30. Additionally, the state's Energy Conservation Policy aims to deliver 744 MU of energy savings by FY27, while the Clean Mobility Policy 2025–30 seeks to catalyze approximately ₹50,000 crore in investments, thereby strengthening Karnataka's position as a premier destination for clean energy investment and manufacturing.
Shri Santosh Kumar Sarangi, Secretary, Union Ministry of New and Renewable Energy, stated that India’s energy journey is entering a decisive phase focused on building a resilient, integrated, and investment-ready ecosystem.
